channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Manifestantes protestam contra Tarcísio na porta de clube do Sindicato dos Metalúrgicos de Osasco
item.description: Protesters demonstrated against Governor Tarcísio de Freitas and state deputy candidate Rogério Lins at the entrance of the Metalworkers' Union club in Osasco. The protest occurred during the launch of Lins' candidacy, with accusations of betrayal toward peripheral communities and criticism of violence in São Paulo. Demonstrators claimed the alliance between Lins and Tarcísio symbolizes the abandonment of favelas and working-class neighborhoods.

item.title: Ao vivo: Flávio Bolsonaro faz 1º ato de campanha em Copacabana
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) launched his presidential campaign with the first act in Copacabana, Rio de Janeiro, on Sunday (Aug. 16, 2026). Supporters gathered at 10 a.m. at Posto 5, chosen as his hometown and the Bolsonaro family’s electoral stronghold. The senator was joined by allies, including state deputy Douglas Ruas (PL), candidate for governor of Rio, on the sound truck.

item.title: Lula faz primeiro evento de campanha à reeleição no berço político do PT, em São Paulo
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva officially launched his re-election campaign in São Bernardo do Campo, the PT’s political birthplace, alongside Fernando Haddad and Geraldo Alckmin. The event marks the start of permitted electoral activities, including rallies and online propaganda, while TV and radio ads begin only on August 28. Other leading candidates also launched campaigns in key regions, except Ronaldo Caiado.

item.title: Tarcísio inicia campanha com discurso voltado às mulheres
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicans) launched his re-election campaign for São Paulo governor in an event in Osasco, delivering a speech focused on women. Unlike in 2022, when he campaigned alongside Jair Bolsonaro, this time he did not have the presence of Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), the Bolsonarist presidential candidate. The event signaled a strategic shift in political messaging, aiming to broaden appeal among female voters.

item.title: Simone Tebet alfineta bolsonaristas em evento com Lula: ‘Gritam Barrabás’
item.description: Simone Tebet criticized Bolsonarists during an event with Lula in São Bernardo do Campo, accusing them of shouting 'Barrabás' when speaking of Christ and defending only 'their own family'. She claimed the progressive camp truly defends family values. The event marked the official start of the 2026 election campaign, with expectations of 20,000 attendees at Vila Euclides Stadium.

item.title: Tarcisio diz que ‘errou e acertou’ no governo e vê segurança pública como ‘grande desafio’ de SP
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas acknowledged mistakes and successes in his administration, identifying public security as a major challenge, and pledged to create the Police House and expand AI-powered cameras. He became emotional while reflecting on his four-year term and announced new commitments in Osasco, including a specialized medical outpatient clinic and the Mother’s House for atypical families. The campaign launch focused on women voters amid rising femicides and his lower popularity among women, according to polls.

item.title: Renan se coloca como "único que pode combater Lula e Flávio"
item.description: Renan Santos (Missão) positioned himself as the only candidate capable of combating corruption from Lula and the Bolsonaro family, claiming he can end corruption in the center and the STF. His statement marked the start of the official campaign period, with a launch event in São Paulo in front of USP’s Law School. According to a Quaest poll, Lula leads with 38%, Flávio Bolsonaro with 31%, and Renan Santos with 4%, placing him third despite being the least known candidate.

item.title: Tebet: “Adversários de Lula falam de Cristo, mas gritam Barrabás”
item.description: Simone Tebet (PSB) criticized Lula's opponents for claiming to defend Christian values while, in her view, 'shouting Barabbas,' linking them to pro-U.S. demonstrations and the defense of personal interests over the Brazilian family. She praised social programs like Bolsa Família and Minha Casa Minha Vida as true defenders of the family and called for Lula's re-election, as well as the election of Fernando Haddad and Marina Silva, framing the 2026 election as a defense of democracy, sovereignty, and social rights.

item.title: Presidente do BNDES defende ‘tomar café, almoçar e jantar’ para reeleger Lula
item.description: BNDES President Aloizio Mercadante advocated for Lula's re-election at the PT campaign launch in São Bernardo do Campo, using the phrase 'have coffee, lunch, and dinner' as a metaphor for collective effort. He criticized Flávio Bolsonaro, pointing to the weakening of BNDES under Jair Bolsonaro’s government and defending national sovereignty against proposals to share strategic information with foreign powers. Held at the historic Vila Euclides Stadium — a symbolic site of Lula’s early labor activism — the event aimed to evoke nostalgia while projecting a forward-looking vision for Lula’s 2026 campaign.

item.title: Haddad critica prioridades do governo paulista no 1º vídeo de campanha
item.description: In his first campaign video, Fernando Haddad (PT) criticized the priorities of Governor Tarcísio de Freitas' administration, claiming it favors wealthy businessmen and large corporations over the public. He questioned the state of public services, citing declines in education, healthcare, and security, and noted that São Paulo's growth has been only a quarter of the national average despite being the federation's richest state.

item.title: Zema envia aviãozinho a Lula: “Lugar de intocável é na cadeia”
item.description: Romeu Zema, the presidential candidate from the Novo party, launched his electoral campaign with a social media video showing him sending a paper airplane toward Lula, carrying the message "The untouchable belongs in jail". The gesture is a direct provocation against the former president and current Workers' Party candidate, reflecting the ideological confrontation tone of the 2026 campaign.

item.title: Governo de SP: Tarcísio lança campanha em Osasco e Haddad vai a evento de Lula no ABC
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas launched his campaign in Osasco, meeting with women from the productive sector and highlighting support for atypical mothers, becoming emotional during the event. Fernando Haddad, alongside President Lula, attended a rally in São Bernardo do Campo at the Vila Euclides stadium—a historic PT rally site—to bolster support for the federal government. Both candidates officially began their 2026 race for the São Paulo state government.

item.title: Nikolas lança vídeo presidencial para concorrer a deputado federal
item.description: Federal deputy Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG) released a campaign video intended for his re-election to Congress, but its nationalistic tone and focus on broad Brazilian issues make it appear as if he is running for president. The video has caused confusion due to its presidential-style presentation, despite his actual candidacy being for a federal deputy seat.

item.title: STF reforça vigilância sobre ameaças contra ministros da Corte
item.description: STF ministers express concern over rising threats against them and their families as the 2026 electoral campaign begins, attributing the trend to political exploitation of the Court’s unpopularity. Intelligence bodies from the STF and government are monitoring social media, turning serious threats with execution capacity into formal PF investigations. Two years ago, VEJA reported the PF was already investigating over a hundred such threats, many from individuals angered by Court rulings.

item.title: Ambulantes vendem camisas de R$ 50 a R$ 70 e boneco de Lula a R$ 100
item.description: Street vendors sell Lula-related merchandise outside the 1º de Maio stadium in São Bernardo do Campo during the event that opens Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's 2026 re-election campaign. Customized shirts range from R$50 to R$70, bags are sold for R$40, and a Lula figurine costs R$100. The rally launches the slogan 'Brazil ready for more', highlighting PT achievements and signaling priorities such as national defense, rare earth exploration, and full-time education, amid ongoing tensions with the United States.

item.title: O voto ainda está em aberto (por Gaudêncio Torquato)
item.description: The Quaest poll reveals that while Lula leads with 38% and Flávio Bolsonaro with 31% in prompted voting, 51% of voters cannot name a candidate in the spontaneous question, indicating the vote has not yet solidified. Despite the polarization between the two main candidates, 30% of voters admit they could change their choice, and the runoff shows a technical tie (43% to 40%), leaving room for shifts in the seven weeks before the first round.

item.title: Primeiro dia de campanha em SP tem Tarcísio em Osasco e Haddad com Lula no ABC; veja as agendas
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas and Fernando Haddad launched their street campaigns for the 2026 São Paulo elections this Sunday. Tarcísio held events in Osasco, including a meeting with productive sector women and a rally at Sindmetal, while Haddad began in São Bernardo do Campo alongside President Lula. The governor emphasized women-focused policies and became emotional over the support, recalling his narrow win in Osasco in 2022.

item.title: Vídeo: Neta de Lula diz que sofreu “hate” do PT após gravar sobre política
item.description: Bia Lula, a communicator and granddaughter of President Lula, said she faced 'hate' from the Workers' Party after posting political videos, claiming the party fears young left-wing voices gaining traction on social media. She argued the PT needs more young voices to connect with younger voters and criticized older members for resisting new leadership. Bia spoke at the launch of Lula’s re-election campaign in São Bernardo do Campo.

item.title: Ao vivo: Lula faz 1º ato de campanha em São Bernardo do Campo
item.description: Lula launched his 2026 re-election campaign with an event in São Bernardo do Campo, a historic site of his union activism in the 1970s and 1980s. The rally brought together PT militants, social movements, and allied parties, aiming for 20,000 attendees, and unveiled the slogan 'Brazil ready for more', emphasizing priorities such as national defense, rare earth exploitation, and full-time education.

item.title: Brasil brilha na série mista e leva 2° ouro no Mundial de Ginástica
item.description: Brazil won two gold medals at the 2026 Rhythmic Gymnastics World Championships in Frankfurt, winning both the five-ball and mixed series (three hoops, two clubs) with identical scores of 29.450 points — the highest of the year. This historic achievement marks the first time a non-European or Asian nation has won gold in the event, and the first for the Americas. After a shaky start on day one (26.800 points), the team rose from 8th to first place, with athletes Maria Eduarda Arakaki, Maria Paula Caminha, Mariana Gonçalves, Julia Kurunczi, Sofia Pereira and Nicole Pircio securing Olympic berths for 2028.

item.title: Com decisão de última hora, Pablo Marçal lança candidatura à Presidência
item.description: Entrepreneur and influencer Pablo Marçal secured his presidential candidacy registration through a last-minute court injunction that temporarily overruled his ineligibility, allowing him to leave União Brasil and return to PRTB, the party that nominated him for São Paulo mayor in 2024. Despite the judicial decision, Marçal remains ineligible until 2032 due to TSE convictions for paying supporters to create viral video edits, which violates electoral law. The TSE will still review the final validity of his candidacy.

item.title: De olho no voto feminino, Tarcísio escolhe Osasco para abrir campanha
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas launched his re-election campaign in Osasco, targeting the female vote with promises to enhance women's safety through shelters and electronic ankle monitors for aggressors, while pledging to expand TEA Centers and 'Houses for Atypical Mothers' across the state. According to the Vox Brasil poll, he leads with 53.7% voter intention, compared to Fernando Haddad's 34%, suggesting a likely first-round victory.

item.title: Flávio inicia campanha: “Estou mais que preparado para comandar esse país”
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) launched his presidential campaign stating he is 'more than prepared to lead this country' and has received the 'Bolsonaro mantle' from his father, former president Jair Bolsonaro. The statement was made during a live broadcast on the first official day of the campaign, accompanied by the caption 'let the games begin'.

item.title: Lula pede voto "no desejo, no sonho e na crença" do eleitor
item.description: Lula urged voters to base their vote on their own desires, dreams, and beliefs, emphasizing they should choose who best represents their hopes for Brazil, not just for him. He stated his goal is to improve the country for the people, not for himself, and declared that Brazil is ready to advance with citizens' support.

item.title: Governo vê risco eleitoral em repercussão de decisão de Moraes sobre sigilo da fonte
item.description: The Lula government sees electoral risk in Minister Alexandre de Moraes's decision to break source secrecy, fearing it will be exploited by international right-wing sectors as a freedom of expression argument to generate social media disturbances and interfere in the 2026 elections. The decision, which authorized an operation against a former Maranhão secretary identified as a source in an investigation into alleged monitoring of Minister Flávio Dino, drew immediate criticism from the press and Brazilian right-wing sectors, but was defended by Moraes as necessary to investigate persecution crimes, emphasizing that source secrecy cannot shield criminal activity. The government believes new digital interference attempts will occur through the end of the second round.

item.title: Começa agora a campanha: um guia para vencer as eleições presidenciais
item.description: The text critiques Lula's campaign, emphasizing his obsession with denying crimes from Operation Lava-Jato, the perceived authoritarian alliance with the Supreme Federal Court and Alexandre de Moraes, and the defense of economically flawed policies that repeat past mistakes. It also highlights a tendency to prohibit, intolerant identity politics, and a 'us vs them' narrative as key factors alienating undecided voters, evoking left-wing authoritarianism and attacking fundamental freedoms.

item.title: Conheça o Estádio 1º de Maio, palco do evento de Lula
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) will launch his 2026 re-election campaign with an event at the Municipal 1º de Maio Stadium in São Bernardo do Campo (SP), a historic site of labor strikes in the 1970s and 1980s where he led metalworker mobilizations. The event, scheduled for August 16, 2026, symbolizes his return to the origins of his political and union trajectory, in the same venue that once hosted assemblies of up to 150,000 workers. Now managed by São Bernardo FC, the stadium has undergone modernization while retaining its status as a symbol of Brazil’s labor movement and democratic struggle.

item.title: "Direita Raiz", diz Caiado em primeiro vídeo de campanha nas redes
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) launched his first campaign video, presenting himself as "root right-wing" and criticizing the PT. He emphasized his 40-year political trajectory and announced a caravan in Luziânia, marking the start of official electoral propaganda. The Quaest poll shows Lula at 38%, Flávio Bolsonaro at 31%, and Caiado at 4% in the 2026 first-round scenario.

item.title: Ex-BBBs se lançam candidatos nas eleições de 2026. Saiba quem são
item.description: Several former Big Brother Brasil contestants are running in the 2026 Brazilian elections, including Jean Wyllys (PT, SP), Adrilles Jorge (União Brasil, SP), Lucas Penteado (PT, SP), Matteus Amaral (PP, RS), Gyselle Soares (PP, PI) and Vivian Amorim (União Brasil, AM). Many of them have prior political experience or were finalists/runners-up on the reality show. Their candidacies highlight the growing intersection between TV fame and political life in Brazil.

item.title: Lula abre campanha em estádio que marcou sua trajetória sindical
item.description: Lula officially launched his re-election campaign at the 1º de Maio stadium in São Bernardo do Campo, a historic site of his union activism in the 1970s and 1980s. The event drew caravans of PT militants and allied movements, with an expected turnout of 20,000, symbolizing a return to the roots of the labor movement that birthed the PT and CUT. Lula declared this would be his final presidential candidacy, seeking an eighth term.

item.title: PT quer fazer do ABC o maior ato da campanha de Lula
item.description: The PT aims to make the event in São Bernardo do Campo the largest of Lula's 2026 presidential campaign, expecting 20,000 attendees at the Municipal Stadium 1º de Maio. The event seeks to reconnect the party with grassroots mobilization, reinforce Lula's image as a popular leader, and launch the official slogan 'Brazil Ready for More', featuring Janja da Silva and cabinet ministers.

item.title: Zema e Renan Santos preferem mirar críticas a adversários no Instagram
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo) and Renan Santos (Missão) focused their criticisms of Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro mainly on Instagram, with Zema posting 45 and Renan 46 critical contents from June 1 to August 11. Lula was the main target, receiving 149 criticisms versus 59 against Flávio, while Caiado (PSD) was the only candidate to prioritize X, with 38 posts there compared to 24 on Instagram.

item.title: ‘Lula tem ajudado muito mais o PT do que o PT o tem ajudado’, diz um dos fundadores do partido
item.description: Djalma Bom, a former metalworker and one of the PT's founders, says Lula has helped the party more than the party has helped Lula, arguing the PT needs a 'new conception' to open up to society. He criticizes the party's aging structure and the left's current lack of intellectuals, recalling his decades-long alliance with Lula from 1970s union struggles to imprisonment under the dictatorship. Lula's campaign event on April 16 at Vila Euclides stadium will feature Djalma and other comrades in a nostalgic act, focusing on reclaiming key moments from Lula's political history.

item.title: Governo Lula mantém sigilo sobre retorno de policiais cedidos a tribunais
item.description: The Ministry of Justice has placed under secrecy the list of federal police officers assigned to courts who are expected to return to the force, according to Estadão. The directive, communicated in a June memo, was interpreted by PF and judiciary members as a possible retaliation against delegate Thiago Marcantonio, who works in the office of Minister André Mendonça of the STF. The move raises concerns about political interference in institutional independence.

item.title: "Caça à leoa": Celina começa campanha nas redes falando sobre ataques
item.description: Governor Celina Leão (PP) launched her re-election campaign in the Federal District via social media video, stating she will focus on solving DF's problems — especially in health — and ignore adversaries' attacks, which she likened to a 'lioness hunt'. She cited redirecting BRB funds and Brasília festival resources to health and reducing SUS waitlists. Michelle Bolsonaro, Bia Kicis, and Damares are expected to attend her first campaign rally in Ceilândia on Sunday, August 15.

item.title: Flávio diz que recebeu "manto de Bolsonaro" em 1ª fala durante campanha
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) launched his presidential campaign by claiming he received the 'Bolsonaro mantle' from his father, Jair Bolsonaro, in a video released on Sunday. He stated the 2026 election is not about Bolsonaro vs PT, but about Brazil winning or the PT destroying the country. According to a Quaest poll, Lula (PT) leads with 38% voting intention, followed by Flávio at 31%, with the PT's advantage narrowing from 9 to 7 percentage points.

item.title: Campanha eleitoral nas ruas e propaganda virtual começam neste domingo
item.description: The electoral campaign for Brazil's 2026 elections officially began this Sunday (16), allowing candidates to conduct in-person activities such as caravans, marches, and leafleting between 8 a.m. and 10 p.m. Virtual propaganda is also permitted, marking the official start of campaigning both on the streets and online.

item.title: Zema inicia disputa eleitoral com provocação a Lula nas redes
item.description: Romeu Zema, former governor of Minas Gerais and presidential candidate for the Novo party, launched his campaign with a provocative social media video featuring a paper airplane bearing the message 'Untouchables belong in jail! I’m coming… Zema' directed at President Lula. The post, made on Sunday (August 16), coincided with the TSE’s authorization for electoral propaganda in public spaces and online, signaling the official start of the presidential race.

item.title: Romero Jucá registra candidatura após Dino suspender condenação
item.description: Romero Jucá (MDB-RR) registered his candidacy for federal deputy from Roraima on Saturday, the 15th, after Supreme Court Minister Flávio Dino suspended the effects of a conviction that could have made him ineligible. A provisional injunction from the STF and STJ nullified the conviction's effects, allowing Jucá to run in the 2026 election. The candidacy was first reported by O Antagonista.

item.title: Em 1ª live de campanha, Renan fala em vingança e critica Lula e Flávio
item.description: Renan Santos (Missão) officially launched his presidential campaign in a YouTube live stream that peaked at 27,000 viewers, advocating for harsher police operations against organized crime and proposing a 'Nuremberg of the Favelas' to posthumously prosecute deceased criminals. He accused Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro of corruption, linking Lula to alleged INSS fund diversions and Flávio to investigations involving Daniel Vorcaro, and suggested a potential runoff between them could be 'settled at Vorcaro’s house in Trancoso'.

item.title: Programa de Flávio dá continuidade à transição energética de Lula 3
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) proposes continuity in Lula's energy transition, focusing on biofuels, decarbonization, and modernization of the electricity sector. His government plan aligns with the current petista administration's guidelines, including ethanol and biodiesel expansion, strengthening RenovaBio, and investing in energy storage.

item.title: Plano de Flávio não menciona Petrobras, e Lula cita estatal 11 vezes
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro’s 75-page government plan for the 2026 presidential race makes no mention of Petrobras, despite advocating for expanded gas exploration in the pre-salt, fracking, and reviving the National Privatization Program. In contrast, Lula’s plan references the state oil company 11 times, positioning it at the core of Brazil’s energy policy. Flávio argues the state’s role is to ensure the country functions, not to act as a businessman, and proposes case-by-case evaluation of privatization.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro deve muito à Michelle, sua madrasta
item.description: The rapprochement between Flávio Bolsonaro and his stepmother Michelle Bolsonaro was described by Noblat's panel as a staged, short-lived arrangement, taking place during a barbecue at the party headquarters in Brasília. While it boosted Flávio’s standing among evangelicals and women in the Quaest poll, the alliance is seen as a survival tactic for him and a long-term investment for Michelle, who aims to serve eight years in the Senate from the DF to position herself for a 2030 presidential run. Flávio risks losing his seat and special STF immunity if defeated in 2026.

item.title: Tensões diplomáticas tendem a agravar distanciamento comercial entre Brasil e Argentina
item.description: The strategic partnership between Brazil and Argentina, Latin America's most important, is at its worst point in decades due to diplomatic tensions between Argentine President Javier Milei and Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, marked by mutual insults, ambassador withdrawals, and a cooling of trade flows. Although Argentina's economic crisis is reducing its import demand, Brazil has been disproportionately affected by the decline in Argentine imports compared to other partners like China and the U.S. While Brazil-Argentina trade fell 18% in the first half of 2026, Argentine exports to China and the U.S. surged by 42% and 63%, respectively, signaling a strategic shift away from Brazil, particularly in the automotive sector where cross-border production chains are being disrupted.

item.title: A inesperada vaia a Flávio Bolsonaro no Rio
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro faced unexpected jeers in Rio de Janeiro following the revelation of his proximity to Daniel Vorcaro, linked to the sponsorship of the film 'Dark Horse'. The incident, described as a 'displeasure' for the senator, occurred in May and provoked negative reactions even outside direct electoral contexts. The subscriber-only article suggests the episode reflects image wear tied to controversial associations.

item.title: Cleitinho declara patrimônio de R$ 956 mil ao TSE
item.description: Senator Cleitinho Azevedo (Republicanos-MG) registered his candidacy for governor of Minas Gerais with the TSE on August 14, 2026, declaring assets worth R$ 956,564.03. After uncertainty due to personal reasons, including his brother's death, he was confirmed as the party's candidate on August 7, running in a pure ticket with Luís Eduardo Falcão as his running mate.

item.title: “Evidente que vamos mudar a regra”, diz Marinho sobre arcabouço fiscal
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), a presidential candidate, states he intends to replace the current fiscal framework with a new rule aimed at reducing public debt and achieving primary surpluses, though he has not disclosed the formula. Rogério Marinho (PL-RN), campaign political coordinator, confirmed the change is evident and necessary.

item.title: Michelle Bolsonaro registra candidatura ao Senado pelo DF
item.description: Former First Lady Michelle Bolsonaro registered her candidacy for the Senate in the Federal District on Saturday, the 15th, shortly before the TSE deadline. This will be her first run for public office, running under number 222. In the DF, voters will elect two senators in this election.

item.title: Renan Santos critica mais Flávio Bolsonaro do que Lula nas redes
item.description: Renan Santos (Missão) criticized Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) more than Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) on social media between June 1 and August 11, 2024, with 45 posts targeting the senator and 42 targeting the president, including 14 posts that criticized both simultaneously. His criticisms of Flávio centered on corruption suspicions (rachadinha, Dark Horse film funding) and the claim that he 'is not right-wing', while critiques of Lula focused on economic issues such as public debt and social programs. Renan favored Instagram for his statements, where he criticized Lula more, while on X he posted more against Flávio.

item.title: Amiga de Lulinha comprou joias para Marcola de Lula
item.description: Federal Police investigators discovered that lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger paid for two jewelry items selected by Marco Aurélio Santana Ribeiro, known as Marcola, to gift relatives of Lula’s former chief of staff for Mother’s Day 2024. The transactions were revealed via WhatsApp messages and PF investigations, reported by Globo.
